residuals.text: A revoked registry principal maps to a lease holder URN without complaint (observed with a temporary registry: principal:gone with revoked set -> urn:soveraeign:principal:model:gone). The builder did not claim revoked handling and no fixture covers it. sovsession.principals already distinguishes REVOKED, so the mapping could refuse or annotate. Repair belongs inside this concern if the builder judges a revoked holder should not take a lease; otherwise record it as a declared non-check in the module docstring.

contracts/principal.schema.json constrains principal_id only by minLength 1, while the lease holder pattern requires [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ after the kind. A registered id containing '/', ' ' or similar maps to a URN that _validate refuses with a schema pattern error rather than a named refusal. The five ids in the current registry are all safe; this is a gap between two contracts, not a defect in the claimed behaviour.

cleanup_obligations is optional in the schema (not in closure.required); only the command line always writes it (as [] when --cleanup is absent, proven by test). A lease written by any other path is admitted without the key. The schema description says an empty list is itself a claim; absence is not distinguished from an empty claim by the contract, only by the CLI.

Values that are neither principal:<id> nor a URN pass through instance_principal unchanged (documented in its docstring) and are refused by the holder pattern at _validate with a pattern error, not a named code. Consistent with the claim; not a named refusal surface.

The witness probe appended two events (take, release) for lease:probe-x under session witness-b-probe to the shared append-preserving ledger <repo>/.git/sov-sessions/leases.ndjson. No lease is held; the events are not erasable by design.
